hero.subtitle: A fall at a Lompoc store, apartment complex, or public sidewalk can leave you with medical bills and no clear next step. We can help you understand your options with a free consultation. Our team handles premises liability claims in Santa Barbara County.

about.title: Lompoc Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Lompoc's mix of small retail strips along H Street, apartment properties near O Street, and public walkways throughout the city means falls happen for a lot of different reasons — wet flooring, cracked pavement, poor lighting, or a hazard that was never fixed after someone reported it. Under California law, a property owner or manager can be held responsible only if they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and didn't fix it or warn people about it. That's why what happens right after your fall matters: photos of the hazard, names of any witnesses, and a request to preserve store or building surveillance footage can all make a real difference later. We handle premises liability claims directly. Our team can evaluate the details of your fall and explain your options, working on contingency so there's no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Lompoc Premises Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. We can help gather the evidence needed to establish that notice.

items.title: Video Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many properties overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that footage can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar You
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover damages even if you were partly at fault for the fall — your share of fault simply adjusts the final amount.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Lompoc?
items.answer: In most cases you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit under California law. If the property involved is owned by a government entity — a city building or public sidewalk, for example — that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just a few months. Because of that difference, it's worth having someone review the details of where the fall happened as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell at a business on H Street or O Street and no one else saw it?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't automatically end a claim. Photos of the hazard, your own written account while it's fresh, and any store surveillance video can still support your case. We can help identify what evidence is realistically available in your situation.

items.question: Is there a charge to discuss my case with an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free consultation to discuss your fall. Our team generally works on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
